facts.text: Kollwitzplatz was christened on 7 October 1947 after Käthe Kollwitz, the graphic artist who lived nearby until her death.
A bronze sculpture of Kollwitz, based on her self‑portrait, was erected in the square’s center in 1961 and remains a popular climbing spot for children.
During Berlin’s 750th‑anniversary celebrations in 1987, surrounding streets were rebuilt to match their historic appearance as part of a redevelopment plan.
The 2016 action‑thriller *Jason Bourne* filmed a key scene on Kollwitzplatz, though the Berlin exterior shots were actually shot in Kreuzberg.
Residents successfully opposed a planned demolition of the area until the fall of the Berlin Wall, preserving the neighborhood’s historic character.
Kollwitzplatz sits at the heart of the so‑called “Kollwitzkiez,” a neighborhood that has become one of Prenzlauer Berg’s most sought‑after residential areas.
